entry.title: Saved channels and scan memory keep their shape, and the page world s…
entry.content:
Saved channels and scan memory keep their shape, and the page world stops calling chrome.runtime

The worker stored a channel from YouTube as the page sent it, including any field and a blocked flag the page
could set on hub channels. It is now rebuilt field by field: a YouTube channel address, text without markup,
bounded numbers, an avatar only from YouTube's image hosts, and no blocked flag. Scan memory entries and the one-shot
legacy data are shaped the same way, and the country feed takes only country and language codes, since both end up
in a storage key name. The bundle still had three direct chrome.runtime.sendMessage calls that could never run in
the page world: an unused legacy sender, a fallback in the scan memory, and the channel batch, whose data the door
serves only to extension pages. The first two are gone and the batch now says why it has no data.

entry.title: YouTube sends numbers and the worker writes the alert, the opportunit…
entry.content:
YouTube sends numbers and the worker writes the alert, the opportunity and the preferences

A YouTube tab could hand the worker a ready-made alert, whose title and text were stored and shown as given,
opportunity rows with any fields, and scan preferences of any shape. The worker now loads the ASHLYV engine and
rebuilds each one from ids and numbers: the niche and language must exist in the engine, and the niche name, the
bands, the verdict and the alert title and text come from the engine. Dismissing an alert marks it and takes it off
the unread count (it did nothing), a tab opens the hub at most once every 2 s and ten times in 10 minutes, and the
live alert card no longer calls a money helper that never existed.

entry.title: face-api runs in the isolated world, out of YouTube's globals
entry.content:
face-api runs in the isolated world, out of YouTube's globals

face-api 0.22.2 and its TensorFlow runtime ran in youtube.com's page
world, where they sat among the page's globals and any script could read
or replace them. They now load in the isolated world with a small reader,
content/nsp-faces.js, that answers NSP_FACE_DETECT with the face boxes
and the image size for an i.ytimg.com thumbnail; the scan turns those
into the same verdict as before. The bridge no longer publishes the model
folder in the DOM.

Measured in Chrome for Testing on the same eleven thumbnails, including
two with a face: both builds gave the same verdict, face count and
confidence for all eleven (2.6 s in the page world, 3.8 s isolated,
model load included), and faceapi is no longer defined on youtube.com.

entry.title: The bubble asks before it runs on other sites, localhost is two ports…
entry.content:
The bubble asks before it runs on other sites, localhost is two ports, and keys stay out of localStorage

The bubble was a content script on every http and https page, so the
install prompt asked for all data on all sites for a button. It now runs
from the manifest on YouTube and Studio only. Every other site is an
optional host permission: the popup's switch asks Chrome for it from the
click, the worker registers the bubble for all sites once it is granted
(nspBubbleSync on onAdded, onRemoved and startup), and turning the switch
off gives the access back. Alt+X and CHAT still reach the current tab
through activeTab.

The host permissions granted localhost and 127.0.0.1 on any port. They
are now the ports the code calls: 11434 for Ollama and 7788 for the local
voice server. Options accepts only those two Ollama addresses and says
why, and the worker falls back to the default for anything else it finds
stored, with one check shared through NSP_MODELS.ollamaUrl.

Setup copied the OpenAI and Fish keys into localStorage along with the
voice preferences and never removed them. The copy now holds
preferences only, and Setup and the voice document remove keys an older
build left there. The TypeSafe and Vercel AI Gateway fields stored keys
nothing read; they are gone.

entry.title: A grant needs our own control, and the page stores and shows only wha…
entry.content:
A grant needs our own control, and the page stores and shows only what fits

An audit of c756442 found that the spend grant opened on any trusted
click over an element carrying data-nsp-grant: a script on youtube.com
could put the attribute on <body> and turn every click of the user into
45 model calls. The bridge now creates the controls itself when the page
asks (nspGrantControl) and keeps them in a WeakMap no page script can
reach; a grant opens only for a real press on one of them while it is
connected, visible, of a button's size and under the pointer. The bridge
loads before the page world so the SCAN buttons are such controls.

Storage writes from the page went straight into 19 keys with whatever
objects the page sent, among them nsp_selected_model, nsp_pending_action
and ashlyv_nichos, which skipped the niche sanitizer and reached an
innerHTML in ThumbLab. The bridge now hands writes to the worker, which
rebuilds each value against its key's shape (NSP_PAGE_STORE), caps maps,
lists and size, and refuses with the reason. The model, the saved
niches, the switches and the dashboard's hand-off are read only from the
page; the model changes through NSP_MODEL_SELECT on a real press of the
model menu, and the hand-off may only be cleared. Stored conversations
are roles and text under a size cap.

Notifications carried the page's own title and text with the ZERACK
icon. The page now sends a code and numbers, the worker writes the words
and allows three per tab per quarter hour.

The HTML setter removed a block list of tags and let STYLE, SVG,
ANIMATE, SET and USE through; it now keeps an allow list of tags and
attributes and refuses url() in styles. Error messages in the dashboard
and ThumbLab's status label are written as text.

tests/sw-page-writes and new cases in tests/bridge cover each of these
and fail against c756442.

entry.title: The docs describe the boundary as it is now
entry.content:
The docs describe the boundary as it is now

The README said the bridge forwards sixteen message types and that the
worker refuses the agent's tools when the Agent switch is off; neither
was true. It now has a section on who can ask the worker for what: the
door, grants on a trusted press, the worker's own prompts, the one HTML
path into youtube.com and the read-only switches. Line numbers that no
longer point anywhere are gone, and so are the Pollinations and
Openverse hosts the manifest stopped asking for.

CONTRIBUTING said nothing imports Whisper, but the voice falls back to
it; it pointed at a workflow file that is not there; and it listed
MobileNet. It now says what fetch-assets.sh is for, describes the new
smoke checks and tests/, and keeps the steps to switch the workflow on.

entry.title: Drop MobileNet, which nothing loads
entry.content:
Drop MobileNet, which nothing loads

lib/mobilenet held 15 MB, two thirds of the checkout: four weight
shards, TensorFlow.js, MobileNet and a frame page, mnet-frame.html, that
no page, script or manifest entry opens. It was also exposed to every
website as a web accessible resource. The faceless check uses face-api's
tinyFaceDetector, which stays. The history still carries the files; a
fresh checkout no longer does.

entry.title: The hub reads real data or says it cannot
entry.content:
The hub reads real data or says it cannot

ashlyv.js called nine methods ashlyv-api.js never exported, so channel
age, viral metrics, title search, subniches, batch scan, the full
channel scan, REPLICATOR and BRAND answered "API.x is not a function".
Seven more rejected every call because the backend they posted to does
not ship, and the three AI calls sent a message shape the worker does
not read, so they failed even with a provider set up. The channel
scanner that did run was a model inventing RPM and revenue.

ashlyv-api.js is one client over the worker, sendToSW(type, fields),
with an explicit reason for every failure. What can be measured is
measured: channel age from the join date, viral metrics from the real
views and ages of the latest uploads, competitors, gaps and patterns
from a live search, thumbnails in the browser with canvas (contrast,
brightness, saturation, detail, 16:9, the list-size view). What is
generation goes to the model and is labelled as a suggestion; REPLICATE
and BRAND use the worker's tasks, so their prompts exist once for the
hub and the YouTube panel. What a model cannot know (a score per
language, a click rate from pixels, RPM presented as measured) is gone
from the page.

The ?d= parameter let any website open the hub with niches it wrote,
painted with innerHTML: it is removed, and data is painted with
textContent. The popup's watchlist buttons that were only an emoji,
never drawn because their container does not exist, are removed with
their CSS. Two ternaries the purge emptied in the hub and ThumbLab hold
identifiers again.

tests/hub-api.test.mjs fails if ashlyv.js calls a method the client
does not export, if an AI call leaves the worker's message shape, if a
ternary has two empty branches, or if ?d= is read again.

entry.title: Retired models out of every list, and a partial radar says it is partial
entry.content:
Retired models out of every list, and a partial radar says it is partial

Groq retired llama-3.1-70b-versatile and mixtral-8x7b-32768, and Google
retired the Gemini 1.5 family, all in 2025. They were still in the
model picker, the Options dropdown, the Options key test and the tool
pages, and the in-page coach forced gemini-1.5-flash, which the worker
put first in its chain: every Gemini turn began with a failed request.
They are gone from every list. A retired model an older build saved is
mapped to a live one with a warning, and the model a caller names is
ignored: the user picks it in Options.

The country radar dropped the errors of the searches that failed and
answered ok with whatever the others returned, and an answer in a shape
the parser does not know read as "no videos". It now answers partial,
with how many of the searches failed and why, does not cache a partial
feed as the whole market, and reports no_renderers_recognized when every
search answered and nothing could be read. The radar page says so under
the results.

entry.title: Channel stats, uploads and InnerTube searches read what YouTube shows
entry.content:
Channel stats, uploads and InnerTube searches read what YouTube shows

Measured in Chrome for Testing, every InnerTube call from the service
worker got 403: YouTube refuses requests whose Origin is
chrome-extension://, and a worker cannot drop that header. The country
radar, the market search the agent and Studio use, and the corpus
fetch all came back empty. One declarativeNetRequest session rule now
removes Origin from this extension's own requests to youtubei, scoped
with initiatorDomains to the extension id so the page's requests are
never touched. The permission is declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess,
which adds no install warning over the hosts already granted.

The channel stats reader ran regexes over the About HTML and returned
someone else's numbers: for Veritasium it gave 29.7 M subscribers, 172
videos, 55 M views and a join date of "DateText", where YouTube shows
21.3 M, 536, 4.59 B and Jul 21, 2010. The agent was told to trust these
as real. It now reads the aboutChannelViewModel the About panel renders,
in English, and returns numbers, a join date, or an explicit
about_panel_not_found instead of a guess. The Command Center reads the
numeric subscriber count.

The uploads reader dropped views and age on the first visit of a fresh
profile, where YouTube serves a compact layout ("4,7 M", "hace 3 d"). It
reads the accessibility label, which keeps the full words.

entry.title: A script on youtube.com can no longer use the extension's privileges
entry.content:
A script on youtube.com can no longer use the extension's privileges

Any script on youtube.com can post to the page, not only ours, and the
bridge forwarded what it asked for. With the Agent switch off, a page
script could list the URL and title of every open tab, close them, open
any https address, and use the user's OpenAI, Groq or Gemini key as a
free proxy with its own system prompt, model and tools. It could also
set the vision consent flag itself and then make the worker download
four arbitrary URLs.

The service worker now checks the sender of every message at one door.
NSP_MESSAGE_CALLERS names, for each of the 64 message types, who may
send it: a page of this extension, the bridge on youtube.com, the Studio
script or the bubble. Listing, switching and closing tabs, navigating
and reading other sites are for extension pages only. From youtube.com,
spending needs a grant: the worker opens one when it hands the tab a
turn from the chat or the voice, and the bridge asks for one only on a
trusted press (isTrusted) of a ZERACK control marked data-nsp-grant. A
grant is per tab, ends by count and by time, and never adds up. The
page sends a task and data (NSP_AI_TASK); the system prompt, the tools
and the model are the worker's. The bridge forwards a fixed list,
rebuilt field by field, and the consent switches are read only from the
page. Opening a tab from the panel needs its grant, the Agent switch
and a YouTube host, all checked in the worker.

The bundle registered a Trusted Types policy named default that passed
any string, which switched YouTube's own protection off for every script
on the page. It is gone. nspSetHTML parses markup inert through a policy
only its closure holds, removes scripts, frames, handlers and javascript:
links, and moves the clean nodes in.

Four panels always said "no AI provider" because their key getter
returned an empty string; a fifth could not reach the worker at all. The
thumbnail check and the A/B view now measure faces, contrast and
brightness in the browser and show no invented score. Title Lab and the
comment reader ask the model through the worker, labelled as its
opinion, and the comment reader reads the comments YouTube has loaded,
since the Data API key does not ship. The PRO panel read channel age by
asking a model to guess it from the name: its tools now read the real
About page, uploads and search, and the language score is gone. An
unreachable second PRO panel of about 1,000 lines is deleted.

Also: the extension id is no longer published in the DOM, web
accessible resources are only the face-api weights for youtube.com and
the chat for the bubble, both on dynamic URLs, the scan history the
assistant reads comes from the niche index every scan writes instead of
a key nobody wrote, saved niches are rebuilt and deduplicated in the
worker, and Studio's panel is a closed shadow root that answers real
presses only.

tests/ load the real worker and bridge in a Node vm with a fake chrome
and the senders Chrome passes; the smoke runs them, and gains checks for
the door table, for no default Trusted Types policy, and for the bridge
forwarding only what youtube.com has a seat on.

entry.title: Undo what the emoji purge broke: reject lists that matched every video
entry.content:
Undo what the emoji purge broke: reject lists that matched every video

The text purge that turned the smoke green deleted emoji inside regexes
and comparisons, not only in copy. Three reject lists lost their emoji
alternatives and were left with empty ones, and an empty alternative
matches every string: OBVIOUS_REJECT in the faceless filter,
HARD_REJECT, and the sports and news check of the feed fallback all
matched every title. The emoji are back as escapes, so the smoke's emoji
rule still holds.

The RPM trend was stored as an arrow; the purge made all three values
the empty string, so the leaderboard could never show a trend. It is now
stored as an id, up, down, flat or new, with the words kept apart.

The same pass ate the spaces around string literals on 119 lines: search
queries became "history2025", panels read "3/10with traction", and the
Stealth scan toast glued the country to the text. Those lines are
restored from the pre-purge code with the emoji removed and nothing
else. Buttons that were only an emoji (close, drag, save, the drop zone
icon) have text and an aria-label again, and the Studio hook chips say
"has" or "no" instead of relying on colour alone.

smoke.mjs gains a check: no regex literal may have an empty alternative.

entry.title: A bubble on every site that opens a private chat, a voice that hears,…
entry.content:
A bubble on every site that opens a private chat, a voice that hears, and the course inside the assistant

The ouroboros is the new mark: redrawn as vector, it is the toolbar icon
and a 52 px bubble in the bottom-right corner of every page. A click
opens the chat over the page; holding it is hold-to-talk. The chat runs
in a cross-origin frame opened with a one-time token, so a website can
neither read it nor drive it, and its switches refuse clicks while
anything covers it. History lives in IndexedDB on this computer. Typed
commands run at once with no model call; anything else goes to the same
assistant as the YouTube panel, with the model picker, the agent switch
and a Voice history that shows what was heard, done or dropped and why.
Alt+X opens it, and the side panel takes over where pages cannot host
the bubble.

Voice, measured in Chrome for Testing: every spoken confirmation used to
deafen the ear for up to 4.6 s, two quick commands merged into one the
router refused, background speech made hands-free deaf for a minute,
Google rarely wrote the name, and every drop was silent. Now the ear
keeps listening while ZERACK talks and filters its own echo, acts on the
stable interim text (0.65 to 0.88 s median instead of about 1.4 s),
splits merged commands, confirms visible actions with a short sound,
and marks background noise on the bubble. Hold-to-talk answers 0.08 s
after release and caught 6 of 6 phrases in quiet and 4 of 6 under a
narrator, where hands-free caught none. Only phrases that look like a
command beep when ignored, so talk in the room stays quiet.

The course is no longer a page for the owner. It is the assistant's
method: a 33-lesson list in every prompt and a zerackCourse tool that
returns whole lessons with their sources. One brain file feeds the
YouTube panel, the chat and the voice, and each provider now gets a
prompt fitted to its limit instead of Groq silently losing everything
after 9,000 characters. The old knowledge block that contradicted the
course is gone.

Four reviewers found 33 defects; two skeptics each confirmed all 33 and
they are fixed, among them the fetch tool reaching any host, the typed
router hijacking questions, and the bubble covering YouTube's controls.
Smoke green, load checks 8 of 8, router 70 of 71 with no false action.

entry.title: Voice that listens by itself and acts on what it hears
entry.content:
Voice that listens by itself and acts on what it hears

One switch turns the voice on or off: the round button on YouTube, the
dot in the popup, or Alt+Z. The side panel is gone. While it is on, the
microphone stays open in an offscreen document and Chrome's own speech
recognition, handed that microphone track, turns each phrase into text
under a second after it ends. Local Whisper took about 33 seconds per
phrase on a busy machine and misheard short Spanish commands; it stays
only as the fallback when Chrome's recognizer cannot run, and is no
longer loaded otherwise.

A browser command runs as soon as it is heard, with no wake word.
Anything else is dropped unless it starts with oye, hey or the name, and
then it goes to the assistant in the YouTube tab, which is brought to the
front or opened first instead of answering blind from another page.
While any tab is playing sound, commands need the name as well, so a
video cannot give orders. Recognition pauses while ZERACK speaks, so it
never hears itself.

The assistant now decides: when the data it needs is missing it fetches
it with its own tools instead of telling the user which scan to run, and
it no longer asks for location, budget or language before recommending.
Spoken replies are cut to their opening sentences; the full answer stays
in the panel.

A question that reached YouTube within a second of the page loading was
cancelled as a leftover from the previous page. The leftover check now
reads the mark before any turn of this page can write one.

Verified in Chrome for Testing with a fake microphone: with the voice on,
'busca historia para dormir' opened the search, 'oye, abre YouTube' and
'ahora YouTube' opened YouTube, 'me gusta mucho este video' did nothing,
the same search with a tab playing sound was dropped, and 'oye, que
nicho me recomiendas' from a blank tab opened YouTube and came back
answered and spoken. The orb and the popup button switch it on and off,
and it stayed listening for 75 seconds of silence. Router: 65 of 66,
no false actions. Smoke green.

entry.title: A voice for the assistant, and the extension loads in Chrome again
entry.content:
A voice for the assistant, and the extension loads in Chrome again

Two characters in the agent commit broke the whole extension: raw U+FFFF
noncharacters as the top of two regex ranges. Chrome reported the file
as not UTF-8 and refused to load anything, scanner included. They are
escapes now and mean the same range. The smoke gained a check that
decodes every script as strict UTF-8 and rejects noncharacters; it goes
red on the exact bug and names the line.

The voice lives in Chrome's side panel, so the microphone is granted to
the extension and never to youtube.com. Speech to text runs on the local
Whisper model, so audio never leaves the machine. Push to talk is the
default; the wake word is a toggle, off by default, and shows plainly
when it is listening. What the user says goes through the in-page
assistant exactly as if typed, so the agent switch, its step cap and
STOP all apply unchanged. With no YouTube tab it still answers questions.

Voices: the browser voice, free; the ZERACK brand voice on Fish Audio;
OpenAI's onyx; and a local voice server when one answers. The paid ones
are labelled paid and run only while selected. Any failure falls back to
the browser voice and says why once, so the assistant never goes silent.

Setup gained fields for the Fish Audio key and voice, and for Jev through
TypeSafe or Vercel AI Gateway, all optional.

Verified in Chrome for Testing against this tree: the extension loads,
the scanner boots on YouTube, the agent refuses to act while off, a page
script cannot turn it on, turned on from the extension it reads and
clicks, and a spoken question from a fake microphone was transcribed
locally, answered, and sent to Fish with the ZERACK voice.

entry.title: The assistant can act in the browser, behind a switch the page cannot…
entry.content:
The assistant can act in the browser, behind a switch the page cannot flip

A single action tool takes what to do and a target described in words,
and resolves the target on the live page by visible text, label, role,
placeholder or title. Plans run up to 30 steps, an instruction up to 40,
and a visible STOP ends the chain at once. It never types into password,
one time code or payment fields, never acts outside YouTube's hosts, and
stops once to ask before it publishes, deletes, sends or comments.

The switch lives in the popup and defaults to off. The assistant panel
runs inside youtube.com, so a switch there could be flipped by any script
on that page; the bridge now has a read only list, and the page world can
read nsp_agent_enabled but never write it. Every step, alone or inside a
plan, passes through one gate that checks it.

The smoke learned both halves. Its string extractor paired quotes wrongly
around short strings and read the code between two literals as text; it
now matches every literal and filters by length afterwards. And it only
saw storage keys written in quotes, so an object literal write from the
page slipped through green. It now goes red on a page write to a read
only key and names the line.

entry.title: A course inside the extension, built from sources that were checked
entry.content:
A course inside the extension, built from sources that were checked

Six modules and 33 lessons that take someone from zero to a faceless
channel that pays: picking a niche with the scanner, packaging,
production, publishing, reading your own numbers, and knowing when to
stop or double down.

Every lesson carries its sources, 74 in total, each fetched and checked
the day it was written: YouTube Help pages matched on a key phrase, posts
on X confirmed with their author. A claim that could not be sourced was
cut, and one lesson went because its cited post said the opposite.

Progress is saved per lesson in extension storage, survives a reload, and
does not break when lessons are added or removed. Each lesson that uses a
part of the extension has a button that opens it. The popup gets one
COURSE row.

The assistant header also counts an OpenAI key now: the bridge used to
check only Groq, the local model and Gemini, so a user whose only key was
OpenAI saw NO PROVIDER while the assistant answered normally.

entry.title: The project is signed by the brand, not by a person
entry.content:
The project is signed by the brand, not by a person

Copyright now reads ZERACK. Every commit in the history carries the same
name and a neutral address, so cloning the repository does not hand out
the author's real name or the name of the machine it was built on.

entry.title: Park the CI workflow until the token carries the workflow scope
entry.content:
Park the CI workflow until the token carries the workflow scope

GitHub refuses a push that creates .github/workflows from a token without
that scope, so the file waits in ci/ and CONTRIBUTING says how to move it
back in one command.

entry.title: OpenAI joins the cascade, first in line
entry.content:
OpenAI joins the cascade, first in line

The owner has an OpenAI key and the local model is too slow to film
with. OpenAI was the one provider the cascade did not know about.

It is wired the same way as the rest: the key lives in storage, the
model comes from the shared catalog, and it sits first in the fallback
order, so a failure there still falls through to Groq, the local model
and Gemini rather than ending the answer.

Proved with a deliberately wrong key: the request reaches OpenAI in 369
milliseconds and comes back 401, then the cascade carries on and the
assistant still answers from the local model. With a real key the whole
answer lands in about a second.

GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 mini are in the model picker, the key
field is on the setup page, and api.openai.com is in host permissions.
